title: Equivalence-edge subspaces in filtered pointwise colimits of Segal spaces
statement:
Use nested universes, small spaces and coherent diagrams from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], filteredness from [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and Segal objects and their homotopy categories from [lem-coef-complete-segal-quasicategory-comparison]. A Segal object means a simplicial small space $X:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S$ whose consecutive-edge maps $X_n\to X_1\times^h_{X_0}\cdots\times^h_{X_0}X_1$ are equivalences for every $n\geq2$; completeness is not assumed. Write $X_{\mathrm{eq}}\subseteq X_1$ for the union of those path components whose arrows are invertible in the homotopy category $hX$, that is, have a two-sided inverse up to composition homotopies. Every map of Segal objects induces a map of these subspaces. Let $I$ be any small filtered quasicategory and let $i\mapsto X_i$ be a coherent diagram of Segal objects. Suppose the pointwise space colimit $X_n=\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}(X_i)_n$, with its induced simplicial operators, is a Segal object $X$. Then the canonical map of spaces over $X_1$
$$\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}(X_i)_{\mathrm{eq}}\longrightarrow X_{\mathrm{eq}}$$
is an equivalence. No completeness, nonemptiness, discreteness or injectivity condition on the spaces or transition maps is imposed.

source.place: Rezk, A model for the homotopy theory of homotopy theory, Sections 5.3, 5.5, 5.7 and Lemma 5.8, for finite inverse witnesses and the union-of-components definition. The filtered-colimit assertion is an agent argument from these conventions and filtered space finite-limit exactness; not a quoted theorem of Rezk. Online source read, archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical assertion.

proof.text: Use the Segal-space conventions in [lem-coef-complete-segal-quasicategory-comparison]: composition is induced by the Segal equivalences, and invertibility means a two-sided inverse up to composition homotopies. A simplicial map preserves identities, composition and those homotopies, so it preserves equivalence edges. Put A_i=(X_i)_eq and B_i=(X_i)_1. The inclusions form a coherent diagram A_i→B_i and induce A=colim_i A_i→B=colim_i B_i=X_1, factoring through X_eq.

source.place: Sections 5.3–5.8 for inverse witnesses; agent finite-pullback argument using filtered finite-limit exactness

proof.text: For a Segal object $Y$, construct its finite inverse-witness space explicitly, using homotopy limits throughout. Put $U=Y_0\times Y_0$, with coordinates $(x,y)$. In spaces over $U$, let $F$ and $G$ be the pullbacks of $Y_1\to Y_0^2$ along $(x,y)\mapsto(x,y)$ and $(x,y)\mapsto(y,x)$, and put $P=F\times_U G$. Let $T_x$ and $T_y$ be the pullbacks of the vertex map $Y_2\to Y_0^3$ along $(x,y)\mapsto(x,y,x)$ and $(x,y)\mapsto(y,x,y)$. Consecutive edges define maps $T_x\to P$ and $T_y\to P$, ordering the edges of the second map as $(f,g)$ rather than $(g,f)$. Put $T=T_x\times_P T_y$. Define $L_x$ and $L_y$ by pulling $Y_1\to Y_0^2$ back along $(x,y)\mapsto(x,x)$ and $(x,y)\mapsto(y,y)$, and put $H=L_x\times_U L_y$. The two middle faces define $T\to H$, and the two degeneracies define a section $e:U\to H$. Now set $V(Y)=T\times_H U$, with these maps, in spaces over $U$. Its points are $f:x\to y$, $g:y\to x$, two triangle lifts, and paths in the fixed-endpoint mapping spaces from their composite edges to $s_0(x)$ and $s_0(y)$. The Segal condition makes the triangle-lift maps equivalences over $P$; the composition and two-sided-inverse convention of [lem-coef-complete-segal-quasicategory-comparison] therefore says that the image of $V(Y)\to Y_1$ meets exactly the equivalence components. Every displayed object is obtained by finitely many products and homotopy pullbacks from $Y_0,Y_1,Y_2$, and every displayed map comes from simplicial operators, diagonals or permutations. Thus $V$ is functorial on coherent diagrams without choosing composition maps. No contractibility of the inverse-witness space is asserted.

source.place: Sections 5.3–5.8 for inverse witnesses; agent finite-pullback argument using filtered finite-limit exactness

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-spaces-kappa-limit-filtered-colimit] with κ=aleph_0 to each of the finitely many products and pullbacks defining V. The hypothesis is exactly the given filteredness of I, and the pointwise colimit hypothesis identifies the three inputs with X_0,X_1,X_2, compatibly with their face and degeneracy maps. Consequently colim_i V(X_i)→V(X) is an equivalence compatible with the maps to X_1. Every component of a colimit of spaces is represented at a stage: π_0 preserves colimits because maps from a space to a discrete set are exactly functions on its components (apply the colimit universal property to all discrete targets). Concretely, the resulting set colimit is the quotient of the disjoint union of the component sets by the relations induced by arrows of I, so each component of V(X) comes from some V(X_i). Step 2 implies that every equivalence component of X_1 is met by A→X_1.

source.place: Sections 5.3–5.8 for inverse witnesses; agent finite-pullback argument using filtered finite-limit exactness

proof.text: Each A_i is a union of components of B_i, so its diagonal A_i→A_i×^h_{B_i}A_i is an equivalence. Apply [lem-coef-spaces-kappa-limit-filtered-colimit] at κ=aleph_0 to this pullback diagram. It identifies colim_i(A_i×^h_{B_i}A_i) with A×^h_B A; hence the diagonal A→A×^h_B A is an equivalence. This says every homotopy fiber T of A→B is empty or contractible: if t∈T, the diagonal equivalence T→T×T makes the first projection an equivalence with contractible fiber at t, and that fiber is T. Therefore A→B identifies A with a union of whole components of B, rather than merely giving a bijection on selected points.

source.place: Sections 5.3–5.8 for inverse witnesses; agent finite-pullback argument using filtered finite-limit exactness

proof.text: By step 1 this union is contained in X_eq. By step 3 it meets every component of X_eq, and step 4 says it contains each component it meets with its entire homotopy type. Hence A→X_eq is an equivalence. All maps were constructed from the same degree-one cocone, so this is the stated canonical equivalence over X_1. The construction allows empty edge spaces and non-injective transition maps, and never assumes completeness or discreteness. A filtered I is nonempty by definition; this is the only index nonemptiness used.

source.place: Sections 5.3–5.8 for inverse witnesses; agent finite-pullback argument using filtered finite-limit exactness

proof_origin.place: Sections 5.1, 5.3, 5.5 and 5.7, Lemma 5.8, for the Segal inverse convention only. The filtered-colimit argument and finite witness construction are written here by the agent, using the statement of lem-coef-spaces-kappa-limit-filtered-colimit (HTT Proposition 5.3.3.3). No theorem of Rezk is claimed to state the filtered-colimit assertion.
